seo.title: SmoothScroll FAQ: Pricing, Safety, Settings & Troubleshooting | Windows
seo.description: SmoothScroll FAQ for Windows 10 and 11: free, safe, install, step size, easing, per-app and per-monitor profiles, gaming, troubleshooting.

questions.q: Does this work with all apps?
questions.a: SmoothScroll intercepts Windows mouse-wheel input before it reaches applications, so it works across virtually everything—Chrome, VS Code, File Explorer, Office, Adobe apps, and more.

questions.q: Will it drain my battery?
questions.a: No. SmoothScroll uses near-zero CPU when idle and only runs its 120 Hz loop while a scroll movement is active. On low battery, the Settings window also surfaces a gentle hint if you want to pause smoothing temporarily.

questions.q: Is it safe? What does it install?
questions.a: The Windows installer runs per-user with no administrator rights required. It places smoothscroll-app.exe and uninstall.exe in %LOCALAPPDATA%\SmoothScroll. No kernel driver, Windows service, or network listener is installed.

questions.q: Is SmoothScroll safe?
questions.a: Yes. SmoothScroll is a user-space desktop app with no service, daemon, system driver, network listeners, or telemetry. See the privacy page for full data-handling details.

questions.q: How is this different from Windows' built-in smooth scrolling?
questions.a: Windows' built-in smooth scroll is app-specific and inconsistent. SmoothScroll applies one configurable easing engine across apps—with six presets, per-app and per-monitor profiles, and an instant hotkey toggle.

questions.q: Does it work with gaming mice or high-DPI devices?
questions.a: Yes. SmoothScroll reads actual hardware wheel deltas—including standard notched wheels and high-resolution wheels—and applies smoothing on top.

questions.q: Can I disable it for specific apps?
questions.a: Yes. Right-click the tray icon and flip the switch next to the active app, or open Settings → Apps → Per-app assignments and set that app to Disabled (pass-through).

questions.q: What Windows versions are supported?
questions.a: Windows 10 and Windows 11 (64-bit) are fully supported.

questions.q: Is there a Linux version?
questions.a: Not published yet. SmoothScroll currently ships public installers for Windows 10 and 11; future releases are announced on the GitHub Releases page.

questions.q: How do I uninstall?
questions.a: Uninstall SmoothScroll from Windows Settings → Apps → Installed apps, or run %LOCALAPPDATA%\SmoothScroll\uninstall.exe. To remove saved preferences and logs as well, delete %APPDATA%\SmoothScroll.

questions.q: Does this work with UWP / WinUI apps?
questions.a: By default, Auto-disable in Windows apps pauses smoothing in built-in Windows apps (such as Notepad, Settings, Photos, Calculator, and Microsoft Store) that already animate scrolling natively. Turn on Settings → Behavior → Force Smooth on All Apps to override this, though some WinUI surfaces may still ignore synthetic wheel events.

questions.q: Will anti-cheat flag this?
questions.a: SmoothScroll never injects into game processes, passes raw input to elevated (administrator / UAC) windows, and automatically pauses smoothing when a known game is in the foreground.

questions.q: How is this different from Logi Options+ or Razer Synapse?
questions.a: SmoothScroll works with any mouse Windows recognizes rather than one vendor's hardware. Because it runs at the OS input layer, your scroll feel stays identical when you switch mice.

questions.q: Can I sync scroll direction with my Mac?
questions.a: Yes. Reverse direction can be toggled globally in Scroll → Direction or inside individual scroll profiles.

questions.q: Is SmoothScroll really free? What's the catch?
questions.a: Yes. The Windows release is free, with no ads, no account requirement, and no feature paywall. Installers are available on smoothscroll.top and GitHub Releases.

questions.q: Does SmoothScroll need an account or collect telemetry?
questions.a: No account, no telemetry, no analytics. Settings live locally in %APPDATA%\SmoothScroll\SmoothScroll\config\settings.json and logs stay on your device.

questions.q: How do I install SmoothScroll on Windows?
questions.a: Download SmoothScroll_1.36.0_x64-setup.exe from smoothscroll.top or GitHub Releases and run it. Installation is per-user with no admin prompt, and a quick welcome screen lets you start with recommended defaults in one click.

questions.q: What do step size, animation time, and easing actually change?
questions.a: Step size sets how many pixels each wheel notch travels, animation time sets how long the motion takes to settle, and easing sets the deceleration curve. Tune distance first, then duration, then curve.

questions.q: Which settings should I try first?
questions.a: Start with Default (144 px step, 220 ms animation, Quintic Out easing) or click the six presets at the top of the Scroll tab. Lower step size in Advanced if pages move too far, or raise animation time for a longer glide.

questions.q: What do acceleration and tail-to-head ratio do?
questions.a: Max acceleration caps how much consecutive wheel ticks multiply speed during fast spins, while max velocity sets when acceleration peaks. With Exponential Out easing, tail-to-head ratio sharpens deceleration—higher values start faster with a longer slow tail.

questions.q: Does SmoothScroll work with precision touchpads?
questions.a: Yes. Settings → Devices includes a dedicated Precision touchpad section with live input-source detection, a smoothing toggle, pixel multiplier, and acceleration factor.

questions.q: Does it support high-refresh-rate (120/144 Hz+) monitors?
questions.a: Yes. The engine schedules smooth output aligned to high-refresh displays, and Monitor profiles let each screen use its own scroll profile.

questions.q: What are scroll profiles, monitor profiles, and per-app assignments?
questions.a: Scroll profiles store custom step size, animation time, acceleration, easing, direction, and zoom settings. Under Apps, you can assign a profile to a monitor, to an application across all monitors, or to an application on one specific monitor (priority: App on Monitor > App > Monitor > Global default).

questions.q: What is the global hotkey and can I change it?
questions.a: Ctrl + Alt + S toggles smooth scrolling system-wide from anywhere. You can turn it off or record a new shortcut in Settings → Behavior → Hotkey combination.

questions.q: Will Ctrl + wheel zoom still work in browsers and design tools?
questions.a: Yes. SmoothScroll preserves Ctrl, Shift, and Alt modifiers during wheel events, and Scroll → Smooth zoom offers dedicated Ctrl + Wheel zoom smoothing (off by default). For untouched ticks in a specific tool, set its profile's Wheel compatibility to Native/raw or set the app to Disabled (pass-through).

questions.q: Does SmoothScroll affect gaming performance or FPS?
questions.a: No. Game mode automatically pauses smoothing whenever a game in your Known games list is focused, restoring raw notches for weapon wheels and scopes.

questions.q: Is there a macOS version?
questions.a: Not published yet. SmoothScroll currently ships public builds for Windows 10 and 11; check GitHub Releases for announcements.

questions.q: How is SmoothScroll different from other free scrolling utilities?
questions.a: It works with any mouse Windows recognizes, installs per-user without drivers or background services, supports per-app and per-monitor profiles, includes Game mode auto-bypass, and ships with zero telemetry.

questions.q: SmoothScroll isn't smoothing one app — how do I fix it?
questions.a: Check three things: (1) whether the app is set to Disabled (pass-through) in the tray panel or Settings → Apps; (2) whether it runs as Administrator (elevated windows receive raw input unless SmoothScroll also runs elevated); and (3) for built-in Windows apps, enable Settings → Behavior → Force Smooth on All Apps.

questions.q: How do I back up or move my settings to another PC?
questions.a: Open Settings → About → Backup & restore, click Export settings to save a JSON file, and use Import settings on your other PC.

questions.q: Do I need to change the Windows 'lines to scroll' setting?
questions.a: No. SmoothScroll controls scroll distance directly via Step size, so you can keep the default Windows mouse wheel setting.

seo.title: Privacy Policy — SmoothScroll
seo.description: SmoothScroll collects no personal data: no account, no telemetry, no analytics, no ads. Settings and logs stay on your device.

privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains what information SmoothScroll ("we", "the app") and the website smoothscroll.top ("the website") handle, why, and what choices you have. In short: the app is designed to work offline on your device. We run no server that receives your personal data, and we do not collect, sell, or share personal information.

sections.heading: Scope
paragraphs: This policy applies to the SmoothScroll desktop application, whether obtained from smoothscroll.top, GitHub Releases, or the Microsoft Store, and to the smoothscroll.top website. It does not cover third-party services, which are governed by their own policies (see "Third-party services" below).

sections.heading: Information we do not collect
paragraphs: The app is built so that your activity never reaches us:
bullets: No account or registration — the app works without sign-up.
No analytics or usage statistics — we never learn which apps you use, which files you open, or which websites you visit.
No telemetry or automatic crash uploads in release builds.
No tracking cookies set by us — the website is static.

sections.heading: Data stored on your device (local data)
paragraphs: Everything the app needs stays locally on your machine:
bullets: Settings: your scroll preferences, per-monitor profiles, and per-app assignments, saved to %APPDATA%\SmoothScroll\SmoothScroll\config\settings.json on Windows.

Logs & icon cache: diagnostic logs (rotated daily and pruned after 7 days) and cached local app icons in %APPDATA%\SmoothScroll\SmoothScroll\config\logs; open the folder anytime from Settings → About → Open log folder.
sections.outro: This data is never transmitted to us. You can view, export, edit, or delete it at any time; uninstalling the app and deleting %APPDATA%\SmoothScroll removes all local data.

sections.heading: Update checks
paragraphs: The app contacts GitHub Releases (github.com) on launch and when you click Check now in Settings → About to check whether a signed update is available. As with any standard HTTPS request, GitHub receives your IP address and standard request headers. No personal or usage data is sent.
If you installed the app through the Microsoft Store, updates are delivered by the Store itself.

sections.heading: Third-party services
paragraphs: The app and website link to or load resources from a small number of third-party services under their own privacy policies:
bullets: GitHub Releases — installer downloads and version checks are served by GitHub.
Buy Me a Coffee — clicking the support button opens buymeacoffee.com in your browser.
VietQR — opening the Support card in Settings → About may load a bank transfer QR image from img.vietqr.io.
GitHub Issues — bug reports and feature requests you submit on GitHub are public under GitHub's terms.

sections.heading: Microsoft Store
paragraphs: When you obtain the app through the Microsoft Store, Microsoft independently processes account and store telemetry under the Microsoft Privacy Statement. We only see aggregate, non-identifying install counts.

sections.heading: Website and server logs
paragraphs: The website is a static export hosted via GitHub Pages. The hosting provider may process standard technical access logs (such as IP address, user agent, and requested path) for security and delivery. We do not use these logs to profile visitors.

sections.heading: Legal bases (GDPR)
paragraphs: For visitors in the EU/EEA: we do not process personal data on our own behalf. The third parties listed above process limited technical request data as independent controllers under their own policies.

sections.heading: Children's privacy
paragraphs: The app and website are not directed at children, and we do not collect personal data from anyone, including children under 13.

sections.heading: Data security
paragraphs: Because your settings and logs stay on your device, we hold no user database. Local configuration files are stored in your Windows user profile and protected by your OS account permissions.

sections.heading: International data transfers
paragraphs: Third-party services such as GitHub and Microsoft operate globally and may process technical request metadata outside your country, including in the United States, under their respective safeguards.

sections.heading: Your rights
paragraphs: Depending on your jurisdiction (such as GDPR or CCPA), you may hold rights to access, correct, or erase personal data. Because we store no personal data about you, deleting your local files erases all app data immediately.

sections.heading: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: We may update this policy when app behavior changes. The latest revision date appears at the top of this page.

sections.heading: Contact
paragraphs: Questions or requests? Email nguyentruongk530042003@gmail.com or open an issue at github.com/quangtruong2003/SmoothScroll.

seo.description: How SmoothScroll turns wheel input into 120 Hz eased scrolling on Windows: presets, easing curves, per-monitor and per-app profiles, tray controls, and shortcuts.

hero.title: See how SmoothScroll
hero.subtitle: A tab-by-tab guide to every setting, preset, tray control, and shortcut in SmoothScroll v1.36—so you can dial in the exact scroll feel you want.

bigPicture.title: The big picture
bigPicture.subtitle: Three steps run for every wheel notch at 120 Hz. What smooth scrolling does at each stage is shown below.

steps.title: 1. Intercept
steps.description: A low-level Windows mouse hook (WH_MOUSE_LL) captures each raw wheel notch and its Ctrl/Shift/Alt modifiers before apps see it.

steps.title: 2. Smooth
steps.description: Your active profile—matched by app and monitor—interpolates the distance along Exponential, Cubic, Quintic, or Linear easing while stacking momentum on fast spins.

steps.title: 3. Emit
steps.description: Smooth pulses fire at 120 Hz to the window under your cursor. Games, elevated admin windows, discrete controls, and pass-through apps receive untouched native ticks.

tabs.title: Every tab in the app
tabs.subtitle: Double-click the tray icon (or right-click → Open Settings) to follow along. The sidebar also lets you switch Light / System / Dark theme and 14 display languages.

sections.label: Scroll
sections.intro: Enable smoothing, pick from six one-click presets, and set scroll direction, zoom, and easing curve. Distance and speed sliders live in Advanced.

settings.name: SmoothScroll (Master switch)
settings.what: Turns the smoothing engine on or restores native Windows scrolling immediately.
settings.why: Lets you A/B test in one click without quitting the app.
settings.tip: Press Ctrl + Alt + S anywhere—or left-click the tray icon—to toggle instantly.

settings.name: Presets
settings.what: Six one-click feel presets: Slow, Default, Fast, Snappy, Mac-like, and Linear.
settings.why: Updates step size, animation time, max velocity, and max acceleration together.

settings.name: Reverse direction
settings.what: Inverts vertical mouse-wheel scrolling (natural-style, like a trackpad or macOS).
settings.why: Keep muscle memory consistent if you switch between a Mac and Windows.

settings.name: Animation time
settings.what: Enables timed eased motion; turn off for instant accelerated jumps. Duration is tuned in Advanced.
settings.why: Quickly compare animated glide against immediate distance scaling.

settings.name: Smooth horizontal wheel
settings.what: Applies smoothing to physical horizontal wheels and tilt-wheel input.
settings.why: Smooths wide spreadsheets, timelines, and canvas pans.

settings.name: Convert Shift + Wheel to horizontal
settings.what: Explicitly remaps vertical Shift + Wheel notches into horizontal scroll events.
settings.why: Handy in apps that don't natively treat Shift + Wheel as horizontal scroll.

settings.name: Invert horizontal direction
settings.what: Flips the direction of smoothed horizontal wheel and Shift + Wheel scrolling.
settings.why: Match horizontal pan direction to your preference.

settings.name: Smooth zoom
settings.what: Applies dedicated smoothing to Ctrl + Wheel zoom in browsers and design tools.
settings.why: Off by default so standard stepped zoom stays crisp unless you opt in.

settings.name: Invert zoom direction
settings.what: Flips Ctrl + Wheel so scrolling up zooms out instead of in.
settings.why: Fixes tools whose zoom direction feels backwards to you.

settings.name: Smooth easing
settings.what: Applies the selected deceleration curve to each scroll movement; off uses a linear ramp.
settings.why: Deceleration is what makes scrolling settle naturally instead of stopping cold.

settings.name: Easing curve
settings.what: Four deceleration shapes—Exponential Out, Cubic Out, Quintic Out (default), and Linear—with a live curve preview.
settings.why: Quintic Out gives a soft Mac-like landing; Cubic Out feels tighter.
settings.tip: Quintic Out has the smoothest tail for everyday browsing and reading.

sections.label: Devices
sections.intro: Shows your live Detected input source (Mouse wheel, High-resolution wheel, or Precision touchpad) and tunes touchpad smoothing separately from mouse wheels.

settings.name: Smooth touchpad scrolling
settings.what: Applies SmoothScroll easing to precision touchpad gestures. Turn off to use native app touchpad handling.
settings.why: Keeps mouse-wheel smoothing active even if you prefer Windows' native touchpad feel.

settings.name: Pixel multiplier
settings.what: Scales raw pixel deltas coming from the precision touchpad.
settings.why: Balance touchpad travel speed against your mouse wheel.

settings.name: Acceleration factor
settings.what: Boosts fast two-finger flicks on the touchpad. Set to 0 to disable touchpad acceleration.
settings.why: Cover long documents quickly while keeping slow drags pixel-accurate.

sections.label: Advanced
sections.intro: Dial in exact scroll distance, animation duration, momentum caps, and wheel compatibility mode. Every slider has a one-click reset button.

settings.name: Step size
settings.what: Pixels scrolled for each physical wheel notch.
settings.why: Higher values cover more page per notch; lower values give finer line-by-line control.
settings.tip: Try 90–110 px for dense code editors, or 180–220 px for long articles and PDFs.

settings.name: Animation time
settings.what: How long each scroll movement takes to settle.
settings.why: Longer durations glide further; shorter durations feel immediate and crisp.
settings.tip: 160–200 ms feels snappy for coding; 350–500 ms feels closer to a Mac trackpad.

settings.name: Max acceleration
settings.what: Upper cap on the momentum multiplier when you spin the wheel rapidly.
settings.why: Lets fast spins fly down long files without losing control.

settings.name: Max velocity
settings.what: Maximum scroll speed threshold before acceleration reaches its peak.
settings.why: Keeps rapid consecutive flicks predictable and bounded.

settings.name: Tail to head ratio
settings.what: Shapes how steep the deceleration tail is when Easing curve is set to Exponential Out.
settings.why: Higher values launch faster and glide out longer (ignored by Cubic, Quintic, and Linear).

settings.name: Wheel compatibility
settings.what: Selects Smooth pulses, Preserve whole wheel steps, or Native/raw output.
settings.why: Fixes DAWs (such as REAPER) or CAD tools that expect whole 120-unit wheel steps instead of sub-notch pulses.
settings.range: Smooth pulses / Preserve whole wheel steps / Native/raw

sections.label: Apps
sections.intro: Tailor scrolling per application and per display. Priority order: App on Monitor > App > Monitor > Global default.

settings.name: Scroll profiles
settings.what: Create named profiles with independent step size, animation time, velocity, acceleration, easing, direction, wheel compatibility, and zoom sensitivity (0.25–4.00×).
settings.why: Switch apps without ever touching global sliders.
settings.tip: Inside the profile editor, click Apply preset… to start from Slow, Mac-like, or Snappy in one click.

settings.name: Monitor profiles
settings.what: Assign a default scroll profile to each connected display on multi-monitor setups.
settings.why: SmoothScroll switches profiles automatically as your cursor moves between a 4K external monitor and a laptop screen.

settings.name: Per-app assignments
settings.what: Click Assign app to bind a running app (or typed process name) to a custom profile or Disabled (pass-through)—across All monitors or on one specific monitor.
settings.why: Unifies custom per-app profiles and app exclusions in one place, with automatic preset suggestions by app category.

sections.label: Game mode
sections.intro: Automatically pauses smooth scrolling whenever a known game is in the foreground so raw notches go straight to the game.

settings.name: Auto-disable in games
settings.what: Pauses the engine when any listed game is focused and shows a live Active / Inactive status badge.
settings.why: Preserves exact notch-by-notch weapon switching, hotbars, and scope zoom.

settings.name: Known games
settings.what: Ships with 28 popular titles preconfigured, plus a searchable installed-game picker (with icons) and manual .exe entry.
settings.why: Add any game from your PC in two clicks or remove entries you want smoothed.

sections.label: Behavior
sections.intro: Control built-in Windows app handling, global hotkeys, login startup, and accessibility motion rules.

settings.name: Force Smooth on All Apps
settings.what: Overrides Auto-disable in Windows apps so built-in Windows apps also receive smoothed wheel output.
settings.why: Useful if you prefer SmoothScroll's curve over Windows' native UWP/WinUI scroll feel.

settings.name: Auto-disable in Windows apps
settings.what: Automatically pauses smoothing in built-in Windows apps (Notepad, Settings, Photos, Calculator, Microsoft Store) that already smooth scrolling natively.
settings.why: Prevents double-smoothing animations and resumes automatically when you switch away.

settings.name: Global hotkey
settings.what: Enables the system-wide keyboard shortcut to toggle SmoothScroll on or off.
settings.why: Flip smoothing instantly from any app without opening the tray.

settings.name: Hotkey combination
settings.what: Click the recorder box and press any modifier + key (A–Z, 0–9, or F1–F24).
settings.why: Avoid shortcut conflicts with your IDE, browser, or screen-capture tools.

settings.name: Start with Windows
settings.what: Launches SmoothScroll automatically when you sign in to Windows.
settings.why: Set once and enjoy smooth scrolling from the start of every session.

settings.name: Start minimized to tray
settings.what: Keeps the Settings window hidden in the system tray on launch.
settings.why: Pair with Start with Windows for a silent background startup.

settings.name: Respect system Reduce Motion
settings.what: Choose Auto (follow system), Always instant, or Always smooth, with a live OS Reduce Motion status readout.
settings.why: Automatically switches to instant scrolling when Windows animation effects are turned off.

sections.intro: Check for updates, review release notes, open diagnostic logs, re-run onboarding, or back up your configuration.

settings.what: Displays your installed version and lets you check for, download, and install signed updates via Check now.
settings.why: Update in place and restart in one click.

settings.what: Reopens the What's new dialog summarizing Added, Fixed, Changed, and Performance highlights.

settings.why: Grab recent diagnostic logs quickly when reporting a bug.
